subject: general
question: Which seasonal change marks the withdrawal of monsoon in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Southward shift of ITCZ**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The withdrawal of monsoon in India is marked by the **southward shift of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ).**
 
• The ITCZ is a belt of low pressure near the equator where the trade winds converge and plays a crucial role in the monsoon system.
 
• During the withdrawal phase, the ITCZ shifts southward towards the equator, signaling the end of the rainy season.
 
• Withdrawal typically starts in northwest India by early October and progresses southward across the country.
 
• This shift is accompanied by clear skies, a reduction in humidity, and a rise in daytime temperatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ):**

 
 
• The ITCZ is a dynamic region of low pressure near the equator formed by the convergence of northeast and southeast trade winds.
 
• It shifts northward and southward seasonally due to the apparent movement of the sun.
 
• Its position influences the monsoon rains in tropical regions, including India.
 
 
 
• **Indian Monsoon System:**
 
 
• The Indian monsoon is divided into two phases: **onset** (arrival) and **withdrawal** (retreat).
 
• The monsoon onset is driven by the northward movement of the ITCZ, while its withdrawal is linked to the southward shift.
 
 
 
• **Withdrawal of Monsoon:**
 
 
• The withdrawal process begins in northwest India and progresses southward, completing by November.
 
• It is marked by clear skies, reduced rainfall, and a gradual cooling of temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Polar Jet Streams:**
 
 
• These high-altitude winds influence weather patterns but are not directly linked to the withdrawal of the Indian monsoon.
